question: There are two types of links supported in the NTFS file system, ________________.
solution:
The correct answer is __hard links and junctions**(NTFS)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Hard links__ and junctions are two types of links supported in the NTFS file system.
 
• A hard link is a directory entry that associates a name with a file on a file system.
 
• Hard links enable multiple filenames to refer to the same file contents.
 
• A __junction__ is a type of reparse point used for creating directory symbolic links.
 
• Junctions allow linking to directories located on different volumes or paths.
 
• Hard links cannot span multiple volumes, whereas junctions can.
 
• Both types of links enhance the flexibility and functionality of the NTFS file system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Hard Links:**
 
 
• Hard links are created using the "mklink /H" command in Windows.
 
• They allow multiple paths to point to the same physical file.
 
• Deleting a hard link does not delete the actual file unless all hard links to the file are removed.
 
 
 
• **Junctions:**
 
 
• Junctions are created using the "mklink /J" command in Windows.
 
• They enable linking directories for better organization and access control.
 
• Junctions are particularly useful for redirecting folder paths without moving the actual content.
 
 
 
• **Symbolic Links:**
 
 
• Symbolic links (symlinks) are another type of link in NTFS, created using the "mklink" command.
 
• They can point to files or directories, spanning across volumes.
 
• Unlike hard links, symbolic links act as shortcuts rather than direct references to file data.
